extracted.intended_audience: general public; researchers; journalists; policy stakeholders interested in technology and media advocacy
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the mission, history, board, programs, and policy priorities of the U.S. public interest technology advocacy organization Public Knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — freedom of expression, open internet, affordable access
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotes freedom of expression, an open internet, and access to affordable communications tools and creative works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Knowledge pursues this mission through media and social platforms, engagement with the U.S. Congress, federal agencies, court and agency filings, research proposing legislation/regulation, publications (blog posts, opinion pieces, papers), and public convenings and multimedia resources to educate and connect the public to policymaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy focus areas — IP, competition, open standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary involvement in the fields of intellectual property law, competition and choice in the digital marketplace, and an open standards / end-to-end internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These thematic areas guide the organization's litigation, legislative advocacy, research, and proposals; the article lists them as the organization's core substantive domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 230 principles to protect free expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and advocate 'Section 230 principles' intended to protect free expression online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as one of Public Knowledge's nuanced policy proposals; presented alongside other frameworks (digital regulator, algorithmic accountability) as policy-level interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal for a digital regulator
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocates for a proposal for a digital regulator as part of its policy toolkit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a concrete policy idea the organization has promoted; positioned with other institutional reform proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative frameworks for algorithmic accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Develops and promotes alternative frameworks for algorithmic accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as one of the organization's policy contributions to address algorithmic systems and their societal effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy for net neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: As of March 2023, the organization advocates for net neutrality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article states Public Knowledge has played a key role in securing net neutrality rules, indicating both advocacy priority and a record of participation in regulatory outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocates for platform competition as a policy priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among current advocacy areas; informs the organization's positions on antitrust, market structure, and technology policy interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer and broadband privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocates for consumer privacy and has helped secure broadband privacy rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization works with agencies like the FCC and FTC and has a record of involvement in privacy-related regulatory efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadband accessibility and affordability
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotes broadband accessibility and affordability — including improving internet access in tribal communities and working to include broadband funding in infrastructure legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites campaigns and coalition-building (e.g., Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act) and targeted efforts to improve access for underserved communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content moderation policy engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Works on content moderation issues as part of its broader technology and media policy agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among advocacy topics; implies engagement with policy proposals, regulatory filings, and public debate on moderation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive media landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocates for a competitive media landscape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the organization's policy priorities, informing positions on media ownership, platform power, and diversity of outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright reform to benefit artists and creators
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports reforming copyright to benefit artists and creators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as balancing copyright reform with public interest goals; the organization promotes changes to law/policy intended to help creators while protecting public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum management reform for consumer access
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocates reforming spectrum management to help consumers gain wireless access — without losing consumer protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article notes Public Knowledge's role in expanding spectrum access for unlicensed use; this criterion combines technical spectrum policy with consumer-protection considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods — research to propose legislation/regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducts research to propose new legislation, regulations, and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research is described as a core method used to develop policy proposals; this complements litigation, agency filings, and public communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications channels — publications and convenings
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes blog posts, opinion pieces, and papers; hosts convenings and multimedia resources to educate the public and connect them to policymaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These channels are listed as means by which the organization applies its work to current events and engages broader audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: PKTrains — public interest advocate training
rubrics_metrics.description: PKTrains is a public interest advocate training program launched to educate diverse, aspiring public policymakers and provide early-career fellows and interns opportunities to work side-by-side with lawyers and advocates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program goals include training fellows to effectively promote policies that benefit the public; the entry emphasizes experiential learning with the organization's staff.
